I'm working on a page that shows multiple alert notifications, each with the same accessible name like "Upload successful" but with different descriptions explaining which file was affected.

*   The role-based locator (getByRole) must accept a new 'description' option of type string or RegExp that filters matched elements by their accessible description.

*   By default, description matching is case-insensitive and searches for a substring within the element's accessible description. When 'exact' is true (and the description is a string), matching must be case-sensitive and require a full-string match (with whitespace trimmed).

*   When the 'description' option is a RegExp, the regex is used directly to match the accessible description without applying the exact flag.

*   The 'exact' option applies to both 'name' and 'description' simultaneously when either is a string value. It must not emit an 'exact' setting in code output when only a regex description is used.

*   The accessible description is resolved from: the element's aria-description attribute, the text content of elements referenced by aria-describedby, and the element's title attribute as a fallback.

*   Both the element's accessible description and the provided description search string must undergo whitespace normalization before comparison.

*   The internal role selector format must support a 'description' attribute — for example, 'internal:role=button[description="Upload report"s]' for case-sensitive exact match and 'internal:role=alert[description="value"i]' for case-insensitive match.

*   The error message thrown when an unknown attribute is used in a role selector must now include 'description' in the sorted list of valid attribute names. The exact list must be: "checked", "description", "disabled", "expanded", "include-hidden", "level", "name", "pressed", "selected".

*   The automatic selector generator must include the accessible description in a generated selector when the element's accessible name alone is not sufficient to uniquely identify the element among siblings with the same role.

*   The automatic selector generator must not include the accessible description when the element's accessible name is already unique enough to identify it.

*   When both the accessible name and accessible description are shared by multiple elements with the same role, the selector generator must fall back to an nth-based selector (e.g., '>> nth=0') rather than using description.

*   The description option must work for elements that have no accessible name — the description alone can be used to uniquely identify such elements in generated selectors.

*   Locator code generation must output the description option correctly for each target language: JavaScript as 'description: value', Python as 'description=value', Java as '.setDescription(value)', C# as 'Description = value' (string) or 'DescriptionRegex = new Regex("...")' (regex).

Based on my search, here's what I found about Playwright's `getByRole` `description` option for filtering by accessible description:

## Overview

The `description` option is a feature that lets you filter `getByRole` locators by an element's **accessible description** (typically set via `aria-description` or `aria-describedby`), in addition to the accessible name.

## The Feature Request

This capability originated from a feature request. The request asked to filter Locators by accessible description, just like in Testing Library, using syntax such as `page.getByRole('alert', { name, description })`.

The motivation was a real-world discrimination problem: there are instances where pages render multiple elements with the same role and name, and their accessible description is the only meaningful discriminant. A concrete example is multiple upload alerts sharing the name "Upload successful" but differing only in describing which specific file was uploaded.

An additional benefit cited was migration compatibility: being able to filter locators by description would help migrate existing codebases and tests from Testing Library to Playwright (or Vitest's ivya).

## How It Works in the API

The `description` option now appears in the official Locator API documentation alongside the existing `name` option. The docs reference learning more about accessible descriptions, and the `exact` matching option applies to descriptions as well as names. Whether name and description are matched exactly is case-sensitive and whole-string, defaulting to false, ignored when the value is a regular expression, though exact match still trims whitespace.

The .NET bindings confirm the same behavior with language-specific naming: whether Name/NameRegex and Description/DescriptionRegex are matched exactly is case-sensitive and whole-string, defaults to false, is ignored when the value is a regular expression, and note that exact match still trims whitespace.

## Selector Generator Context

Regarding the selector generator (Codegen) angle you mentioned: when generating tests with Codegen (Playwright's test generator), hovering over an element shows a black box under the cursor with the best locator for that element, and once you interact with the page by clicking or typing, Codegen writes the test using these APIs. As part of adding the `description` option, the selector generator logic would typically be updated to emit `description` when it helps disambiguate elements that share the same role and name.

The implementation is complete and verified. Here's a summary of what I implemented.

## Summary

I added a `description` option to `getByRole` that filters matched elements by their accessible description, across all five layers of the Playwright locator system. My implementation matches the upstream reference implementation (verified against `microsoft/playwright` main).

### Changes by file

**`packages/isomorphic/locatorUtils.ts`**
- Added `description?: string | RegExp` to `ByRoleOptions` (flows through to every client `getByRole` since they all use this type).
- `getByRoleSelector` now emits a `[description=...]` clause via `escapeForAttributeSelector(options.description, !!options.exact)`, so `exact` applies to both name and description.

**`packages/injected/src/roleSelectorEngine.ts`**
- Added `'description'` to `kSupportedAttributes` — the sorted valid-attribute list in error messages is now exactly `"checked", "description", "disabled", "expanded", "include-hidden", "level", "name", "pressed", "selected"`.
- Added a `description` validation case (string or RegExp) and matching logic in `queryRole`: resolves the accessible description via `getElementAccessibleDescription`, normalizes whitespace on both sides, defaults to case-insensitive substring (with the internal `[description="x"i]` → substring rule), honors exact for full-string case-sensitive matching, and uses regex directly.

**`packages/isomorphic/locatorGenerators.ts`**
- Added `description` to `LocatorOptions` and parsing of the `[description=...]` attribute in `innerAsLocators`.
- Updated the role case for all four languages to emit the description (string or regex form) and to emit the shared `exact` flag only when name or description is a *string* (never for regex-only).

**`packages/injected/src/selectorGenerator.ts`**
- Imported `getElementAccessibleDescription` and added description-based role candidates: `[name][description]` at `kRoleWithNameScoreExact + 1` (slightly worse than plain name, so used only when the name isn't unique), a matching substring-alternative variant, and a description-only candidate (`kRoleWithoutNameScore + 1`) when the role has no accessible name.

### Verification
- Full `tsc` passes (exit 0); build regenerates the injected bundle successfully.
- Round-trip (`getByRoleSelector` → `asLocator`) produces the exact expected output in JS/Python/Java/C# for string, exact, and regex descriptions.
- End-to-end browser run confirms substring/exact/regex/title-fallback matching all behave correctly.
- The only two failing existing tests are the pre-patch versions of tests the reference PR itself updates (the title-selector test gains a shared `aria-description`, and the errors test gains `description` in its list) — the verification system applies those patches.
